The following text is adapted from Jhumpa Lahiri’s 2003 novel The Namesake. Ashima and her husband, Ashoke, are traveling from the United States to India.

Ashoke puts his hand over hers as the plane begins to [vocab]gather[/vocab] speed. And then Boston tilts away and they ascend effortlessly over a blackened Atlantic.

©2003 by Jhumpa Lahiri
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word “gather” most nearly mean?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gain

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doubt

choices.label: C
choices.text: Welcome

choices.label: D
choices.text: Force

explanation.short: In context, "gather" means gain.
explanation.key_evidence: The plane "begins to gather speed" and then ascends.
explanation.why_correct: The plane is accelerating before takeoff, so "gather speed" means gain speed. The other choices do not fit a plane beginning to move faster.
explanation.detailed: The plane is accelerating before takeoff, so "gather speed" means gain speed. The other choices do not fit a plane beginning to move faster.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. The plane gains speed before ascending.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the sentence suggests doubt or uncertainty.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. The sentence describes acceleration, not welcoming someone.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Force does not fit the idiom "gather speed" in this context.

questions.passage: Research on Chaenocephalus aceratus and other icefishes of the Teleostei class has shown that their hearts are pale due to low levels of myoglobin expression, which was once thought to be related to their polar habitats. Recently, researchers have found that some tropical teleost species (such as Sphaeramia nematoptera) also have pale hearts, raising the possibility that myoglobin deficiency in teleosts could be [vocab]______[/vocab]blank habitat.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: irrespective of

choices.label: B
choices.text: mediated by

choices.label: C
choices.text: predictive of

choices.label: D
choices.text: obscured by

explanation.short: Irrespective of means regardless of: the deficiency may occur in different habitats.
explanation.key_evidence: Tropical teleosts also have pale hearts, although pale hearts had been associated with polar habitats.
explanation.why_correct: The same trait in contrasting habitats supports the possibility that it occurs regardless of habitat.
explanation.detailed: The old explanation tied low myoglobin to polar conditions. Tropical examples remove that proposed habitat restriction. A states that habitat may be irrelevant; the other choices describe control, prediction or concealment instead.

choice_analysis.A: Irrespective of expresses independence from habitat, matching the polar/tropical contrast.
choice_analysis.B: Mediated by would make habitat a controlling influence, contrary to the inference being introduced.
choice_analysis.C: Predictive of would make the trait identify a habitat despite its occurrence in contrasting habitats.
choice_analysis.D: Obscured by describes concealment; the question is whether habitat explains the trait, not whether it hides it.

choices.label: B

questions.passage: Paleontologist Amane Tajika and colleagues analyzed the shells of two marine mollusks called nautilids that were harvested from New Caledonia. questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the student’s hypothesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fijian nautilids generally live at lower depths than New Caledonian nautilids do, though Fijian nautilids migrate to the typical depth of New Caledonian nautilids to lay their eggs.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• - ArcelorMittal Orbit is an artwork by Sir Anish Kapoor and Cecil Balmond. - It is a 375-foot steel tower with a spiraling staircase and working slide. - It is on display in a public park in London, England. - Čumil the Sewer Worker is a work of art by Viktor Hulík. - It is a bronze sculpture of a man emerging from under a manhole cover. - It is on display on a public street in Bratislava, Slovakia.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between ArcelorMittal Orbit and Čumil the Sewer Worker. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ArcelorMittal Orbit and Čumil the Sewer Worker are both on display at public locations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ArcelorMittal Orbit, but not Čumil the Sewer Worker, can be found in London, England.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both ArcelorMittal Orbit and Čumil the Sewer Worker were created by Sir Anish Kapoor and Cecil Balmond.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Čumil the Sewer Worker, a bronze sculpture of a man emerging from under a manhole cover, is on display on a public street.

explanation.short: Choice A identifies the shared public-display status.
explanation.key_evidence: The notes say one artwork is in a public park and the other is on a public street.
explanation.why_correct: The student's goal is to emphasize a similarity. Choice A generalizes the two notes accurately: both works are on display at public locations.
explanation.detailed: The student's goal is to emphasize a similarity. Choice A generalizes the two notes accurately: both works are on display at public locations.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. It states the similarity that both artworks are displayed publicly.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. It emphasizes a difference, not a similarity.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. It falsely says both works were created by the same people.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. It describes only one artwork.
